newsitem.title: USA: NATO said to be preparing new arms proposal.
newsitem.headline: NATO said to be preparing new arms proposal.

text.p: The United States and its allies are preparing a new conventional arms reduction proposal they hope will reasssure Russia about the non-threatening nature of NATO expansion, officials said on Friday.

Washington hoped NATO could agree on the broad outlines of the proposal by early next week but one official told Reuters that differences -- within the adminstration and among allies -- would probably delay agreement for another week.

The proposal concerns modifications in the 1990 Conventional Forces in Europe (CFE) treaty which has already caused the United States, Russia and others who signed the treaty to eliminate more than 58,000 pieces of equipment from their forces in Europe.

"The Russian concern about the military infrastructure in NATO is about Conventional Forces in Europe so there is an opportunity to use this current round of CFE negotiations to address some of Russia's concerns and since CFE is a treaty, it is legally binding," one senior U.S. official told Reuters.

Another official predicted the NATO proposal would contain "significant reductions" in current levels of weapons -- such as armoured personnel carriers, artillery and tanks -- permitted under the CFE.

A third official said: "We all agreed we want this (proposal) to be one of the avenues for reassuring the Russians about NATO enlargement but we also have to protect the future military flexibility of the alliance."
He added that developing the allied proposal "has proven to be somewhat more difficult than we anticipated" because of differences within the administration and among the allies.
